docs.title: RUP documentation and code, from your AI coding agent
docs.text: RUP documentation skill · rup-flow 0.4

docs.title: Document your system and build it from the same models
docs.text:
rup-flow teaches your AI coding agent to turn requirements into RUP models and diagrams. The free edition covers the first disciplines. rup-flow Pro covers the whole workflow, from requirements to code and from legacy code back to models, with evidence for every claim.

Document your first system See what Pro adds

Works with the agent you use Never invents requirements Node.js only

docs.title: One workflow, two editions
docs.text: The free edition is a complete, working sample. It stops where the project gets serious, and tells you so instead of improvising.

docs.title: Free
docs.text:
The simplified domain model, actors, requirements, use cases with their specification statechart, analysis classes and open questions, drawn with PlantUML. MIT licensed.

Start with the free edition

docs.title: Pro
docs.text:
The ranked domain model, every diagram type, design, implementation and traceability, code in both directions, themes, Mermaid, the interactive explorer, stack packs, domain libraries and subagents.

Explore Pro

docs.title: Every statement has a provenance
docs.text: Confirmed by you, assumed by the agent, or open as a question. An assumption is never written as a fact.

docs.title: Unknown rules become questions
docs.text: Missing business rules go to open-questions.md instead of being invented to make a document look complete.

docs.title: The agent says what it did not do
docs.text: Diagrams are not called rendered or checked unless the render ran and the result was looked at. Anything outside your edition is named, not improvised.

docs.title: Your first minute
docs.text:
Prompt
Use rup-flow to document this system in docs/rup, in English:
an online shop where customers place orders for products.

The agent asks only what it cannot know, writes the documents, draws the diagrams and checks the result. Open docs/rup/README.md and follow the links.

Follow the complete quick start →

Current documentation: this site describes rup-flow 0.4. Use the version selector when you operate another release line so commands and configuration match the skill you installed.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: rup-flow is a skill plus a small command line. It has no runtime dependencies and no service of its own.

docs.title: System context
docs.text: Open the PlantUML source

docs.title: Parts
docs.text: Part Responsibility SKILL.md The operating rules and the map from a request to the reference to read references/ Methodology, loaded on demand templates/ Starting content of each artifact, with {{placeholders}} scripts/rup.mjs The CLI: structure, index, render, check, instructions scripts/lib/ Small modules: PlantUML client, use-case index, instruction blocks, edition loader editions.json The catalogue of artifacts and capabilities, free or Pro runtime/compose.yaml The PlantUML container definition .claude-plugin/, install.mjs Adapters for Claude Code and for clients that read .agents/skills

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
• One portable core. The skill follows the Agent Skills format; client specifics live in adapters, never in the skill.
  • The agent analyses, the CLI does the boilerplate. Structure, index, rendering and checks are deterministic code.
  • Honesty over completeness. The rules forbid inventing content, and the CLI refuses what the edition does not include instead of faking it.
  • No dependencies. Node.js 18 or newer is enough.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
1. Move the Unreleased entries of the changelog to a new version section.
  2. Bump the version in package.json, the plugin manifest and SKILL.md.
  3. Merge to main, then tag vX.Y.Z.
  4. The release workflow validates and tests, publishes rup-flow-skill.zip on the GitHub release and regenerates the claude-plugin branch.

docs.title: Continuous integration
docs.text: Job Checks Validate Skill format, manifests, links, no binaries, no Pro templates Test The CLI test suite on Linux and Windows with Node.js 18 and 22 Render init, new use-case, render and check against a real PlantUML server

docs.title: This documentation
docs.text: The site is built with MkDocs Material and published with Mike. The version selector uses the free edition's MAJOR.MINOR. Each approved publication gets an immutable tag and a GitHub release. See Versioning and URLs.

docs.title: Editions and the extension point
docs.text:
There is one CLI. Which edition you run depends on one file.

Open the PlantUML source

docs.title: Detection
docs.text:
At start, the CLI looks for scripts/pro/index.mjs next to itself:

File present Edition Behaviour No Free Runs on its own. Anything outside the edition stops with a message that names Pro. Yes Pro The extension adds capabilities and the CLI uses them.

The extension is not part of this repository. It is added when the Pro package is built.

docs.title: What the extension adds
docs.text:
The extension is a module that the CLI calls at defined points:

Point Free behaviour With the extension Templates Only the free templates exist; init and new use-case skip the rest and count them The remaining templates are present and are written Rendering Default PlantUML look Palettes, Mermaid, PNG previews Use-case index Table Table and the use-case diagrams Commands Free commands Plus themes, explore, scan Configuration Mermaid and non-svg outputs are rejected Accepted

docs.title: The catalogue
docs.text: editions.json lists every diagram, document, workflow and tool with its tier. RUP editions prints it and marks what is available in the installation. The documentation pages for the catalogue are generated from the same list, so the CLI and this site cannot disagree.

docs.title: Rules for contributors
docs.text:
• A capability that is not in the free edition must stop with a message that names Pro and exit with code 1, or appear in the available in Pro line. It never fails silently and is never reimplemented in the free tree.
  • Every new artifact gets an entry in editions.json.
  • Validation rejects Pro templates inside the free skill.

docs.title: Why an overlay
docs.text: The Pro package is the free skill with the extension laid over it, renamed rup-flow-pro. Nothing is forked, so a fix in the free edition reaches both.

docs.title: Trust and data flow
docs.text: rup-flow has no account, no analytics and no remote service of its own.

docs.title: On your machine
docs.text:
It does Where Reads and writes files Inside the folders you point it at: the documentation directory and rup.config.json Sends diagram sources To the PlantUML server you run locally, http://127.0.0.1:8085 by default Pulls a container image The PlantUML image from its public registry, the first time you start the server

Nothing else is sent anywhere.

docs.title: The agent
docs.text: The AI agent you use with the skill (Claude, Codex, Gemini or another) processes your prompts and files under that provider's terms and privacy policy, not rup-flow's.

docs.title: The PlantUML container
docs.text: The bundled compose file publishes the container on 127.0.0.1 only and runs it with PLANTUML_SECURITY_PROFILE=SANDBOX, which blocks file and address access from diagrams. Do not expose that port to a network without adding authentication.

docs.title: Generated documentation
docs.text: It contains whatever you or the code contain. Review it before publishing it, especially output derived from code (paths, configuration, table names).

docs.title: Reporting a vulnerability
docs.text: Use GitHub private vulnerability reporting on the rup-flow repository: do not open a public issue.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
rup.config.json sits in the project root. init creates it; every key is optional because the defaults below apply.

rup.config.json
{
  "project": "my-project",
  "outDir": "docs/rup",
  "docLanguage": "en",
  "codeRoot": "src",
  "paths": {
    "domain": "00-domain-model",
    "requirements": "01-requirements",
    "analysis": "02-analysis",
    "design": "03-design",
    "implementation": "04-implementation",
    "quality": "05-quality"
  },
  "useCaseDir": "use-cases",
  "plantuml": { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8085", "timeoutMs": 30000 },
  "diagrams": { "language": "plantuml", "outputs": ["svg"] },
  "ids": { "requirement": "RF", "nonFunctional": "RNF", "useCase": "UC", "rule": "RN", "decision": "DEC", "test": "TC" },
  "targetStack": { "language": "", "framework": "", "persistence": "", "testing": "" }
}

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Key Default Meaning project folder name Name used in titles outDir docs/rup Root of the documentation, relative to the project root docLanguage en Language of the documents. File names, IDs, front-matter keys and PlantUML identifiers stay in English codeRoot . Where the code lives; used by editions that read or generate code paths.* numbered folders Folder name of each discipline under outDir useCaseDir use-cases Subfolder that holds one folder per use case plantuml.url http://127.0.0.1:8085 Address of the PlantUML server plantuml.timeoutMs 30000 Time allowed for one render request diagrams.language plantuml Diagram language. The free edition supports plantuml diagrams.outputs ["svg"] Render outputs. The free edition supports svg ids.* RF, RNF, UC, RN, DEC, TC Prefixes of the stable identifiers targetStack empty Target stack, read by editions that generate code

docs.title: Precedence
docs.text:
Flags override the file, and the file overrides the defaults:

flags  >  rup.config.json  >  defaults

config prints the resolved result.

docs.title: Changing paths on an existing project
docs.text: Changing paths or outDir after documents exist means moving the folders and fixing the links. Do it as one explicit step and run check afterwards.

docs.title: Settings that belong to Pro
docs.text: The free edition rejects a configuration that asks for a Mermaid diagram language or a non-svg output, and ignores nothing silently: it stops with a message that names Pro. Theme settings are only read by Pro.

docs.title: The documentation
docs.text:
This site lives in rup-flow-docs. Work on a branch, run npm run verify and open a pull request.

Rules that keep the site honest:

  • Document released behaviour of the free edition completely.
  • Describe Pro at feature level only. A reader must not be able to recreate a Pro capability from this site.
  • Examples contain no credentials or private data.

docs.title: The free skill
docs.text:
The skill lives in rup-flow. Pull requests improve the free workflow; capabilities listed as Pro in editions.json are developed elsewhere and are not accepted there.

Check Command Validation and tests npm run check Package the web ZIP node tools/package-web.mjs

Conventional Commits, a branch per change and the CI complete check apply to both repositories. Every behaviour change needs a test and a changelog entry under Unreleased.

docs.title: Reporting a problem
docs.text: Open an issue with the documentation template for this site, or a bug report in the skill repository. Report vulnerabilities privately as described in the repository security policies.

docs.title: Analysis classes
docs.text: The first software structure derived from the use cases: what the user touches (boundary), what coordinates (control) and what holds information (entity).

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
@startuml
!theme plain
hide empty members
skinparam linetype polyline
top to bottom direction

class CheckoutScreen <<boundary>>
class CreateOrderController <<control>>
class Order <<entity>>
class OrderLine <<entity>>
class Product <<entity>>
class Customer <<entity>>

CheckoutScreen --> CreateOrderController
CreateOrderController --> Order
CreateOrderController --> Product
CreateOrderController --> Customer
Order *-- OrderLine
OrderLine --> Product

@enduml

docs.title: Stereotypes
docs.text: Stereotype Role <<boundary>> Interface between the actor and the system: a screen, an endpoint <<control>> Coordination of one use case <<entity>> Domain information, taken from the domain model

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Arrows point down, from boundary to control to entity.
  • One control class per use case.
  • Entity names are the ones in the domain model.

Pro adds one analysis collaboration per use case, with numbered messages, and the analysis card that links it to the requirements and the design.

docs.title: Header
docs.text:
Every PlantUML source starts the same way:

@startuml
!theme plain
hide empty members
hide circle
skinparam linetype polyline

Use top to bottom direction by default. Use left to right direction only for short linear flows of four elements or fewer: wide diagrams shrink to unreadable text when embedded.

docs.title: No colors in sources
docs.text: The free edition renders with the default PlantUML look. Do not write colors or theme blocks into sources. Palettes are a Pro feature applied when the diagram is drawn, so the sources stay clean.

docs.title: Avoiding collisions
docs.text:
1. Keep each diagram to twelve to fifteen elements. Split into views before squeezing.
  2. Group related elements in a package.
  3. Fix the order of elements with hidden links, for example A -[hidden]right-> B.
  4. Hold elements together or apart with together { … } and skinparam nodesep or ranksep between 50 and 80.
  5. Prefer short relation labels; put long text in notes on elements.
  6. Write relations with a direction (Order *-down- OrderLine). A plain -- lets both ends land on the same row.
  7. Avoid relations from one hub to everything; introduce a package.
  8. If lines still cross badly after two adjustments, split the diagram.

docs.title: Sandbox
docs.text: The PlantUML server runs with the SANDBOX profile. Diagrams must not use !include of files or addresses.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text: PlantUML identifiers are English, without spaces (use as), and equal to the names in the model. A title inside a diagram is optional; the Markdown heading names the diagram.

docs.title: Simplified domain model
docs.text: The business concepts of the project and the relations between them. Attributes and importance levels are left out; the entity dictionary carries the detail.

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
@startuml
!theme plain
hide empty members
hide circle
skinparam linetype polyline
top to bottom direction

class Order
class Customer
class OrderLine
class Product
class Address

Order *-- OrderLine
Customer -- Order
OrderLine --> Product
Order --> Address

@enduml

docs.title: How to draw it
docs.text:
• File 00-domain-model/domain-model-simple.puml.
  • Entities and relations only. Choose each relation by meaning: composition only when the part cannot live without the whole.
  • Keep it to twelve entities or fewer; split before squeezing.
  • Names are the business terms recorded in the entity dictionary.

docs.title: Companion documents
docs.text:
00-domain-model/README.md holds the entity dictionary (definition, key attributes, source) and the business rules (RN-xxx).

Pro draws the same model ranked by importance, with attributes and multiplicities, and adds the lifecycle of the entities whose state changes behaviour. See the catalogue.

docs.title: Use-case specification
docs.text: The specification is the behaviour source of truth of a use case: a statechart of the conversation between the actor and the system. The card describes the same paths in words; if they diverge, the specification wins and the card is corrected.

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
@startuml
!theme plain
skinparam linetype polyline
hide empty description

state "createOrder" as createOrder {
  state " " as Basket
  state " " as Checkout
  state " " as Validating
  state " " as Placed

  [*] --> Basket
  Basket --> Checkout : Customer asks to check out
  Checkout --> Validating : Customer confirms address
  Validating --> Checkout : System reports unavailable stock or missing address
  Validating --> Placed : System creates order and reserves stock
  Placed --> [*]

  note on link
    Actor: asks to check out
    System: shows lines, totals and the address form
  end note
}

@enduml

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• A composite state named after the use case; inner states have no visible label.
  • Transitions are the events of the conversation.
  • Notes on transitions narrate what the actor does and what the system answers.
  • Error and cancel paths are explicit transitions.
  • skinparam linetype polyline.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• The main flow reaches the goal and every step has a system response.
  • Every input and every precondition has a failure path.
  • The paths match the flows in the card.

Pro adds the wireframes of the screens of the flow, the analysis collaboration and the design sequence for the same use case, each linked from the card. See the catalogue.

docs.title: Get started
docs.text:
rup-flow is a skill: a folder of instructions and a small command line that your AI coding agent loads on demand. You talk to the agent; the agent follows the skill and runs the CLI.

What you need: Node.js 18 or newer and an agent that reads the Agent Skills format. Docker is optional and only draws the diagrams.

docs.title: What the free edition produces
docs.text:
Discipline Folder You get Domain model 00-domain-model Simplified diagram, entity dictionary, business rules Requirements 01-requirements Actors, requirements catalogue, use-case cards with a specification statechart Analysis 02-analysis Analysis classes (boundary, control, entity) Quality 05-quality Open questions

Design, implementation, traceability, audits and code are part of rup-flow Pro.

docs.title: The prompt
docs.text:
Prompt
Use rup-flow to document this system in docs/rup, in English:
an online shop where customers place orders for products.
Actor: Customer. Requirement RF-001: a customer can place an order for one or
more products. Rules: an order has at least one line; a line quantity cannot
exceed stock.

The more you state, the less the agent has to ask. What you do not state is marked assumed or goes to the open questions.

docs.title: What happens
docs.text:
1. The agent reads rup.config.json, or runs init to create it.
  2. It lists the gaps. Blocking questions (rules that change the model) are asked; the rest are marked.
  3. It writes the domain model, actors, requirements, the use case and the analysis classes.
  4. It renders the diagrams and runs check.
  5. It reports files created, open questions, checks that were not executed and the next step.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
docs/rup/
├── README.md
├── 00-domain-model/   README.md, domain-model-simple.puml/.svg
├── 01-requirements/   README.md, actors.md, requirements.md, use-cases/createOrder/
├── 02-analysis/       README.md, class-diagram.puml/.svg
└── 05-quality/        open-questions.md

Open docs/rup/README.md and follow the links. A complete rendered example is in the repository: examples/shop.

docs.title: Check it yourself
docs.text:
node scripts/rup.mjs check --root .

check reports broken links, unbalanced diagram sources, missing renders and a stale use-case index. It does not prove the UML is semantically correct; look at the rendered images.

Past the first minute: when you ask for design, traceability or code, the agent tells you plainly that it is part of rup-flow Pro and does not invent it.

docs.title: How rup-flow works
docs.text:
you ──► agent ──► SKILL.md + references ──► documents (Markdown)
                      │
                      └──► CLI (rup.mjs) ──► PlantUML server ──► SVG diagrams

docs.title: The skill
docs.text:
SKILL.md holds the operating rules and tells the agent which reference to read for each request. The references (methodology, domain-model, use-cases, diagram-conventions, structure) are loaded on demand so the agent spends its attention on your project, not on boilerplate.

The skill is written once in the open Agent Skills format and adapted per client by small adapters (plugin manifest, installer, instruction files).

docs.title: The CLI
docs.text:
A dependency-free Node.js program does the mechanical work:

It does Command Creates the structure and the configuration init, new use-case Keeps the use-case index in sync with the cards index Draws .puml sources into .svg render Verifies structure, links and diagrams check Writes the block that agents without skills read instructions

docs.title: The operating rules
docs.text:
1. Read the configuration first.
  2. Mark every statement as confirmed, assumed or open.
  3. Never invent permissions, rules, states or attributes.
  4. Write where the configuration says.
  5. Do not claim a diagram is rendered or checked unless it was.
  6. Write documents in your language; keep identifiers in English.
  7. Keep one source of truth per artifact.

See Provenance marks and the architecture.

docs.title: Editions
docs.text: The same CLI runs both editions. rup-flow Pro adds an extension that the CLI loads when it is present; without it, the CLI is the free edition. Read Editions and the extension point.

docs.title: Install rup-flow
docs.text: Pick the client you use. All of them install the same skill.

docs.title: Check the runtime
docs.text:
node --version

The skill needs Node.js 18 or newer. Docker is only needed to draw diagrams (see Render and check diagrams).

docs.title: Choose your client
docs.text:
Claude CodeClaude on the webCodex, Gemini CLI and others

Add the marketplace and install the plugin:

claude plugin marketplace add hector-ae21/rup-flow
claude plugin install rup-flow@rup-flow

Then say "Use rup-flow to ..." or run /rup-flow:rup-flow.

  1. Download rup-flow-skill.zip from the latest release.
  2. In Customize → Skills, upload the ZIP.

The web sandbox cannot reach a PlantUML server on your machine, so diagrams stay as .puml sources there; render them locally later.

git clone https://github.com/hector-ae21/rup-flow
cd rup-flow
node install.mjs --target agents

The skill lands in .agents/skills/rup-flow under your home folder. Use --project <dir> to install it for one project only.

docs.title: Verify the installation
docs.text:
Ask the agent to run the CLI, or run it yourself from the skill folder:

node scripts/rup.mjs editions

The first line says this installation: free. The list below it shows what the free edition includes and what is part of Pro.

docs.title: 1. State the objective
docs.text: One sentence: what the system is for and for whom. The agent restates it before modelling; correct it there.

docs.title: 2. Answer the blocking questions
docs.text: The agent separates questions that change the model (a rule, an actor, a state) from details. It asks the first kind and continues with the rest marked assumed. Anything you do not answer stays in 05-quality/open-questions.md.

docs.title: 3. Review the domain model
docs.text: Open 00-domain-model/README.md. Check the entity dictionary and the business rules. A rule marked assumed is a question for you, not a decision.

docs.title: 4. Review the requirements
docs.text: 01-requirements/requirements.md lists functional (RF-xxx) and non-functional (RNF-xxx) requirements with their origin and who confirmed them. Each RF should have at least one use case, and each use case at least one RF.

docs.title: 5. Review each use case
docs.text: Open the card. Check the main flow, alternative flows, preconditions and postconditions. Open specification.svg: the card and the diagram must describe the same paths; if they diverge, the specification wins.

docs.title: 6. Mark what is reviewed
docs.text: Change status in the front matter from draft to reviewed for the artifacts you accepted. The agent never promotes an artifact on its own.

docs.title: 7. Check
docs.text: node scripts/rup.mjs check --root .

docs.title: Where the free edition stops
docs.text: Design (classes, sequences, data model, deployment), implementation cards, traceability and audits belong to rup-flow Pro.

docs.title: Clients that read Agent Skills
docs.text:
Codex, Gemini CLI and other clients that read .agents/skills use the skill as it is:

git clone https://github.com/hector-ae21/rup-flow
cd rup-flow
node install.mjs --target agents

Use --project <dir> to install into one project, --force to replace an existing install (a backup is kept) and --list to see the targets.

docs.title: Clients that read instruction files
docs.text:
Cursor and GitHub Copilot read instruction files. The instructions command adds or refreshes a delimited block in the file each client loads, without touching the rest of it:

node scripts/rup.mjs instructions --target agents,claude,gemini,copilot,cursor --root .
Target File agents AGENTS.md (Codex, Cursor, Copilot agent, Gemini CLI, Zed, Jules and others) claude CLAUDE.md gemini GEMINI.md copilot .github/copilot-instructions.md cursor .cursor/rules/rup-flow.mdc

Running it again replaces the block between its markers and never duplicates it. Use --skill-path <dir> when the skill is installed somewhere else.

docs.title: Tested clients
docs.text: Claude Code, Claude on the web, Codex and Gemini CLI are tested. Cursor and Copilot are supported through instruction files.

docs.title: Start the server
docs.text:
Diagrams are PlantUML sources. A local Docker container draws them:

node scripts/rup.mjs server up --root .
node scripts/rup.mjs health --root .

health renders a test diagram and prints OK when the server is usable. Stop the server with server down.

The container publishes its port on 127.0.0.1 only and runs with the SANDBOX security profile, which blocks file and URL access from diagrams.

docs.title: Render
docs.text:
node scripts/rup.mjs render --root .

Each name.puml becomes name.svg next to it. Up-to-date diagrams are skipped; use --force to redraw everything, or --path <dir> to render one folder. A file with several @start…/@end… blocks produces name-01.svg, name-02.svg.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
node scripts/rup.mjs check --root .
Message Meaning Fix broken link A Markdown link points to a file that does not exist Fix the link or create the file unbalanced @start/@end A diagram source is cut off Complete the source no rendered SVG A source has no image yet Run render use-case index is stale A card changed since the index was generated Run index unresolved template placeholder A {{name}} is still in a document Fill it in

check --strict turns warnings into a failing exit code, which suits CI.

docs.title: What check does not do
docs.text: It validates structure and links. It does not prove that UML is semantically correct or that lines do not cross. Look at the rendered images.

docs.title: The server is not reachable
docs.text: PlantUML server not usable at http://127.0.0.1:8085. Start Docker, then run server up and health. If the port is taken, change plantuml.url in rup.config.json (the port in it is the one the container publishes).

docs.title: docker compose failed. Is Docker running?
docs.text: Docker Desktop or the Docker daemon is stopped. Start it and retry.

docs.title: A diagram fails to render
docs.text: PlantUML reported a syntax error in this diagram names the file in the render report. Fix the source; do not paste colors or !include lines, the server is sandboxed.

docs.title: ... is part of rup-flow Pro
docs.text: You asked for something this edition does not include: a theme, Mermaid, PNG previews, the explorer, scan and the Pro documents. The message includes the address of the Pro page. See Free and Pro compared.

docs.title: Output directory not found
docs.text: check needs the structure first. Run init.

docs.title: The agent invents things
docs.text: Remind it of the rules: mark every statement as confirmed, assumed or open, and send unknown rules to open-questions.md. If it improvises past what the free edition provides, tell it to name what is missing instead.

docs.title: Paths with spaces on Windows
docs.text: Quote them: --root "C:\My Projects\shop".

docs.title: Add one
docs.text:
Ask the agent: "Add the use case cancelOrder for the Customer", or run:

node scripts/rup.mjs new use-case cancelOrder --title "Cancel order" --actor Customer --package Ordering --goal "Cancel an order that has not shipped" --root .

The command creates the card and the specification diagram, assigns the next UC-xxx identifier and refreshes the index. Names are camelCase: verb plus object.

Flag Meaning --title Human title of the card --actor One or several actors, comma separated --package Group of related use cases --goal The user goal in one sentence --requirement Requirement identifier, RF-001 by default --includes, --extends Names of related use cases

docs.title: Keep the index fresh
docs.text:
The requirements README.md holds a generated table between the markers rup-flow:use-cases. After editing the front matter of a card, run:

node scripts/rup.mjs index --root .

Never edit the block by hand: check warns when it is stale.

docs.title: Write a good card
docs.text:
• One user goal per use case, achievable in one sitting by one primary actor.
  • Flows are tables with Actor and System columns; one step is one interaction.
  • Every alternative flow names the step where it starts, its condition and where it ends.
  • Postconditions are split into success and failure.
  • Anything you did not state goes to Pending with the question.

docs.title: Keep card and specification together
docs.text: The specification is a statechart of the Actor/System conversation. Error and cancel paths are explicit transitions. See Use-case specification.

docs.title: rup-flow Pro
docs.text:
The free edition gets you through requirements. Pro takes the same project the rest of the way: models you can trust, code that traces back to them, and documentation that stays honest as the code changes.

Pro is a separate product. It is not a fork: it is the free skill with an extension laid over it, so everything you learned in the free edition applies. It is described here at feature level; the free documentation covers the shared parts completely.

docs.title: Code to RUP
docs.text: Point the agent at a code base and ask for its documentation. Pro inventories the code, reads the parts that matter and writes the same documentation set, with each claim marked observed and cited as path:line. Business rules it cannot read in the code become questions, not invented requirements.

docs.title: RUP to code
docs.text:
From reviewed models, Pro generates code and tests that follow the conventions of your code base, with a trace link from each class or handler to the requirement and use case it implements. Open questions that affect a use case stop its generation, and nothing outside the requested use cases is written.

The agent runs the build, the tests and the linters of your project and reports the result as it is. Whatever it could not run is reported as unverified.

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text:
When code and documentation both exist and may disagree, Pro produces a table of differences:

Kind Meaning Model ahead The documentation describes something the code does not do yet Code ahead The code does something the documentation does not mention Conflict Both exist and disagree Dead An element that nothing refers to

docs.title: Audit
docs.text: A read-only review of the documentation and its alignment with the code, with findings that carry evidence, severity, impact and a proposed fix. The review states which checks it could not execute.

docs.title: Honest limits
docs.text: Generated code is only as good as the reviewed models and your tests. The audit validates structure, links and traceability gaps; it does not prove that UML is semantically correct.

docs.title: One card per discipline
docs.text: Every use case has a card in requirements, analysis, design and implementation. All four start with the same navigation table, so you move between disciplines without hunting for files.

docs.title: Traceability
docs.text: Each requirement, use case, analysis, design, code location and test sits in one table. Empty cells are gaps that check reports.

docs.title: Consistency
docs.text: Pro treats the models as the single source of truth for what they describe. A change in one artifact is propagated to the dependent ones, and the table is updated in the same change.

docs.text: Pro keeps the same posture as the free edition: no account, no analytics and no remote service. See Trust and data flow.

docs.title: Stack packs
docs.text:
A stack pack fixes how reviewed models become code for one stack: folder layout, naming, error handling, persistence mapping and test patterns. The agent reads the pack that matches your configuration before generating code, and it takes precedence over the generic mapping.

Pack Stack nestjs-prisma TypeScript, NestJS, Prisma and Jest

More packs follow in later releases; they are listed in the changelog.

docs.title: Domain libraries
docs.text:
A domain library is a starting point: a ranked domain model, actors, a list of use cases, entity lifecycles and the questions to ask before using it. Everything in a library is marked assumed; the agent adapts it to your objective and never presents it as your requirements.

Library Domain lms Learning platforms: courses, enrolment, activities, grading, completion

docs.title: Subagents
docs.text:
For clients that support subagents (Claude Code does), Pro includes two:

Subagent Does rup-architect Generates and updates the models and generates code from reviewed models rup-reviewer Read-only auditor of the documentation and its alignment with the code

They run independently, so the review is not written by the one who wrote the documents. Without subagents, the review runs as a separate pass.

docs.title: Palettes and colors
docs.text:

The explorer needs no server: it opens from the file system and loads nothing from the network.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
Run the CLI from the project root. RUP below stands for node <skill-dir>/scripts/rup.mjs, where <skill-dir> is the folder that contains SKILL.md.

RUP <command> [arguments] [flags]

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Effect init Create rup.config.json and the documentation skeleton. Never overwrites a file. new use-case <camelName> Scaffold the requirements card and the specification diagram of a use case, then refresh the index. index Regenerate the use-case index table from the cards. render Draw every .puml source into a .svg through the PlantUML server. check Verify structure, links and diagrams. editions Print what the free edition includes and what is part of Pro. instructions --target <t> Add or refresh the rup-flow block in an agent instruction file. server up / server down Start or stop the PlantUML container. health Verify that the PlantUML server renders. config Print the resolved configuration.

Without a command the CLI prints its usage.

docs.title: Common flags
docs.text: Flag Meaning --root <dir> Project root. Defaults to the current directory. --out <dir> Documentation directory, relative to the root (overrides outDir). --lang <code> Language of the documents (overrides docLanguage). --project <name> Project name used in titles. --plantuml-url <url> Address of the PlantUML server. --force Redraw diagrams that are up to date.

docs.title: init
docs.text:
RUP init --out docs/rup --lang es --project shop

Creates the configuration and the free skeleton. Files that exist are skipped. The report lists what was created and how many artifacts are available in Pro.

docs.title: new use-case
docs.text:
RUP new use-case createOrder --title "Create order" --actor Customer --package Ordering --goal "Place an order"
Flag Meaning --title <text> Title of the card. Defaults to the name. --actor <names> Actors, comma separated. Defaults to Actor. --package <name> Package. Defaults to General. --goal <text> The goal in one sentence. --requirement <id> Requirement identifier. Defaults to RF-001. --includes <names>, --extends <names> Names of related use cases. --id <UC-xxx> Force the identifier instead of the next free one.

The name must be camelCase made of letters and digits. The command fails otherwise.

docs.title: render
docs.text:
RUP render --path docs/rup/00-domain-model --force
Flag Meaning --path <dir> Render only this directory. --force Redraw everything.

Exit code is 1 when any diagram fails.

docs.title: check
docs.text: --strict makes warnings fail the command. Without it, only errors do.

docs.title: instructions
docs.text:
RUP instructions --target agents,claude,gemini,copilot,cursor

Without --target it lists the targets. --skill-path <dir> sets where the block says the skill lives.

docs.title: server
docs.text: Needs Docker with Compose. The port comes from plantuml.url.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Done. 1 A check failed, a render failed, or the command stopped (invalid input, missing server, a capability that is part of Pro).

docs.title: Capabilities that are part of Pro
docs.text: These flags and commands stop with a message that names Pro and its address: themes, explore, scan, --theme, --font, --font-size, --color-*, --preview-png, --outputs with png or html, and --diagram-language mermaid. See Free and Pro compared.

docs.title: Folder structure
docs.text:
<outDir>/                              default docs/rup
├── README.md                          index
├── 00-domain-model/
│   ├── README.md                      dictionary and rules
│   └── domain-model-simple.puml/.svg  entities and relations only
├── 01-requirements/
│   ├── README.md                      generated use-case index
│   ├── actors.md
│   ├── requirements.md                RF / RNF
│   └── use-cases/<name>/
│       ├── README.md                  card
│       └── specification.puml/.svg    behaviour (source of truth)
├── 02-analysis/
│   ├── README.md
│   └── class-diagram.puml/.svg
└── 05-quality/
    └── open-questions.md

A use case is named in camelCase (createOrder) and keeps that name as its folder.

docs.title: What each folder is for
docs.text: Folder Purpose 00-domain-model The business concepts, their definitions and the rules that constrain them 01-requirements Who uses the system, what it must do, and each use case as a card plus a specification 02-analysis The first software structure: boundary, control and entity classes 05-quality What is still unknown

docs.title: Folders created by Pro
docs.text: 03-design and 04-implementation do not exist in the free edition, and 05-quality gains the project profile, traceability table, audit and decision records. The numbering is kept so a project can move to Pro without renaming anything. See The complete documentation set.

docs.title: Sources and renders
docs.text: Every diagram is a .puml source with its .svg next to it. Markdown links to the SVG with a relative path. .rup-render-state.json in the documentation directory records the last render so unchanged diagrams are skipped.

docs.title: Front matter
docs.text:
Every Markdown artifact except the index READMEs starts with a block like this:

---
id: UC-001
name: createOrder
title: Create order
actor: Customer
package: Ordering
status: draft
origin: requirements
sourceOfTruth: model
requirement: RF-001
includes: validateStock
extends:
---
Key Values Meaning id UC-001 and so on Stable identifier name camelCase Use-case folder name title text Human title actor names, comma separated Primary actors package text Group of related use cases status draft, reviewed, approved Review state; never promoted by the agent origin requirements Where the content came from sourceOfTruth model The model leads; code, if any, must follow it requirement RF-001 Requirement the use case serves includes, extends use-case names Relations drawn in use-case diagrams

The use-case index and check read id, title, actor, package, status, requirement, includes and extends.

docs.title: Identifiers
docs.text:
Prefix Meaning RF-001 Functional requirement RNF-001 Non-functional requirement UC-001 Use case RN-001 Business rule Q-001 Open question

Never reuse or renumber an identifier. Mark a withdrawn one retired. The prefixes come from ids in the configuration.

docs.title: Provenance marks
docs.text:
Every statement in a document carries one provenance. This is what keeps the documentation honest.

Mark Meaning Who sets it confirmed You said it The agent, only for what you stated observed Found in the code, cited as path:line The agent, when it reads code (Pro) assumed Proposed by the agent The agent open A question The agent, in open-questions.md

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
1. An assumption is never presented as confirmed.
  2. An unknown business rule goes to open-questions.md, not into the model.
  3. The agent never invents permissions, rules, states or attributes to make a document look complete.
  4. An assumed item stays assumed until you confirm it.

docs.title: In practice
docs.text:
The entity dictionary and the business-rule table have a Source column. A rule without a source is assumed. Open questions record who asked, when and what they block.

Observed claims need code, which is the job of the code-to-RUP workflow in rup-flow Pro. In the free edition, statements are confirmed, assumed or open.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Changes of the free skill. The format follows Keep a Changelog and the project uses Semantic Versioning.

rup-flow becomes a free edition plus a paid one. This repository now holds the free edition; rup-flow Pro is a separate private product that extends it. Releases up to 0.3.3 remain available under the MIT license they were published with.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• editions command and editions.json: a catalogue of every diagram, document, workflow and tool, marked free or Pro.
  • An extension point: when scripts/pro/index.mjs is installed next to the CLI, the CLI loads it; the free edition runs without it.
  • The full user documentation is now a versioned site, https://hector-ae21.github.io/rup-flow-docs/.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The free edition keeps the simplified domain model, actors, requirements, the use-case requirements card with its specification statechart, the analysis classes and the open-questions list, rendered with PlantUML in its default look.
  • Generated documents and CLI output point to Pro where a capability is not included.
  • The documentation moved from the GitHub documentation to the documentation site; the documentation is disabled.

docs.title: Removed (now part of rup-flow Pro)
docs.text:
• Themes, palettes, colors and fonts; Mermaid; PNG previews; the interactive explorer.
  • The ranked domain model, entity lifecycles, use-case diagrams, wireframes, collaborations, design, implementation, quality and traceability artifacts.
  • Code to RUP (scan), RUP to code, drift detection, audit, and the rup-architect and rup-reviewer subagents.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • The generated claude-plugin branch carries a square 512 px icon at .claude-plugin/icon.png, which the plugin directory asks for. It is drawn by the same code as the SVG icon and exists only in that branch; main still has no binary files.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • The CLI help describes the four cards of a use case, and CONTRIBUTING.md documents the repository branches.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • The plugin is published from its own branch, claude-plugin, generated on every release tag. It holds only the skill, the two agents and the manifests, so the directory scan no longer reads the installer, tests, workflows or tooling. The repository marketplace installs from that branch. New tools/build-plugin.mjs and a publish workflow, with tests.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Removed every name and mechanism the directory scan reads as sensitive data leaving the machine: a variable in the SVG parser, and the release workflow, which now publishes through the official script action with its logic in a tested module. Validation fails if such names or environment reads appear in code, workflows or manifests.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• One card per discipline for every use case (requirements, analysis, design, implementation and tests), each starting with the same navigation table, plus the implementation card with code and tests tables.
  • index command and generated block in the requirements README: use-case table with links to every discipline, the general use-case diagram (actors outside the system boundary, use cases grouped in packages, include and extend) and one diagram per actor. new use-case takes --package, --goal, --includes and --extends; check warns when the index is stale.
  • Component diagram template (PlantUML and Mermaid) and its section in the design README.
  • Explorer: global search across the text of every diagram, grouping by discipline or by use case, previous and next navigation, links between the diagrams of one use case, a Document tab that renders the cards and follows their links, relation tracing with direct or all-reachable depth, PNG and SVG export, copy source and link, full screen, keyboard shortcuts and richer deep links.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • The example shop now has four use cases in two packages and two actors, and a component diagram.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • The user documentation moved to the GitHub documentation; the README is now a short pitch with install steps that links to it. The repository keeps only the gallery images.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Removed the gallery browser option and turned the repository commands in AGENTS.md into npm scripts, the last two texts the directory scan read as a credential leaving the machine.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Renamed identifiers and literals that the directory scan misread as credential handling (variables named key, the SVG namespace URL, the --chrome option).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • The plugin tree has no binary files, no process.env reads and no listing-only fields in plugin.json, so the directory scan has nothing to report: the icon PNG and explorer screenshots moved to the docs-assets branch, the icon and URLs are set in the submission portal, the CLI reads only flags and rup.config.json, PlantUML requests live in their own module, and the release workflow no longer runs Node. Validation enforces these rules. Added PRIVACY.md.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Compatibility table: Codex and Gemini CLI are marked as tested by the maintainer; Cursor and Copilot remain untested.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Portable across agents: install.mjs --target claude|agents|codex|all (installs into .claude or the .agents/skills location used by Codex and similar clients) and rup.mjs instructions --target ... (marked, idempotent blocks for AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, Copilot and Cursor).
  • AGENTS.md for agents working on the repository, docs/other-agents.md with a compatibility table, and docs/architecture.md with the layers and how to add a client.
  • SKILL.md frontmatter now carries license, compatibility and metadata, and validation enforces the Agent Skills naming rules and a single version across files.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Directory validation holds that were avoidable: the Docker server command no longer forwards the whole environment, CI waits for the server through the CLI instead of curl, and gallery SVGs have short path lines.
  • Release title is the tag alone, and a deleted release can be recreated from its tag with workflow_dispatch.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• rup-flow skill: requirements → RUP, code → RUP, RUP → code, sync and audit workflows.
  • Fixed documentation structure with configurable output directory, folder names, language and identifier prefixes.
  • CLI (init, new use-case, scan, render, check, server, health, config) with no dependencies.
  • PlantUML rendering to SVG through a Docker server (sandbox profile, loopback only).
  • Mermaid as an alternative diagram language (diagrams.language), rendered by a pinned mermaid-cli container.
  • Eight color presets plus custom palettes, fonts and level colors (theme), applied at render time.
  • diagrams.outputs: svg, png previews and an interactive explorer.html (pan, zoom, search, relation highlighting, source, dark view, deep links).
  • explore and themes commands; tools/build-gallery.mjs regenerates the documentation images.
  • Agents rup-architect and rup-reviewer.
  • Claude Code plugin and marketplace manifests, installer, web ZIP packaging and icon generator.

docs.title: Between 0.3 and 0.4
docs.text: Version 0.4 split the project into a free edition and rup-flow Pro. If you used themes, Mermaid, the explorer, code scanning, design, implementation or traceability artifacts with 0.3, those are part of Pro now. Files you already generated stay in your project; the free check keeps working on them. Releases up to 0.3.3 remain available under the MIT license they were published with.

docs.title: Versioning and URLs
docs.text:
Skill versions, documentation lines and publication revisions answer different questions:

  • Skill version: which exact release of the skill is installed?
  • Documentation line: which compatible MAJOR.MINOR contract describes it?
  • Publication revision: which approved snapshot of these pages produced the current wording and images?

docs.title: MAJOR.MINOR controls the site
docs.text:
The version selector and the canonical address use the skill's MAJOR.MINOR. Compatible patches update the same line instead of creating a new copy of the site.

Skill line:        0.4.x
Validated skill:   0.4.0
Version selector:  0.4
Canonical path:    /rup-flow-docs/0.4/

docs.title: Aliases
docs.text:
Alias Points to latest The newest documented line stable The newest documented line that is not a preview

The site root redirects to latest.

docs.title: Publication revisions
docs.text: Each approved publication of these pages gets an immutable tag and a GitHub release. A later editorial fix is a new revision in the same line; it never rewrites an earlier one.

docs.title: Which version do I have?
docs.text:
node scripts/rup.mjs config

does not print the version; read metadata.version in SKILL.md, or the version of the plugin manifest.
